newsitem.title: INDIA: India guerrillas kill 11 troops in premier's visit.
newsitem.headline: India guerrillas kill 11 troops in premier's visit.

text.p: Tribal separatists ambushed and killed 11 paramilitary soldiers as Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral toured a troubled hilly region, police said on Thursday.
Separatist violence has hit five states in the area.
At the same time, six people were injured in a bomb blast elsewhere in the northeastern state of Manipur, where Gujral is expected on Thursday.
Seven soldiers died immediately in Wednesday's ambush, third day of Gujral's five-day tour. Four others died from wounds on Thursday, officials said.

Four more members of the attacked convoy escaped without injury in the assault by suspected Meitei guerrillas in the state bordering Burma near Wangchuk in the Thaubal district, some 40 km (30 miles) from the state capital Imphal.
Gujral, who was far from the location of both attacks, said the killings of security men were "very unfortunate."
He said in Agartala, Tripura's capital, that peace was necessary for the development of the region where separatists accuse New Delhi of ignoring the local economy.
Military officials in the eastern city of Calcutta said the ambush was probably the work of the Meitei tribe, a warrior community living in the highlands of the state.
